summary: A satirical piece describing local sports associations' rollout of wellness programs, which began September 15, 2023, in team sports. It pokes fun at yoga, meditation, tai chi, infused water and healthy snacks replacing traditional drills, pep talks and game-day food. Coaches' earnest quotes contrast with players' discomfort, bad results and cravings for nachos.
one_line: Satirical article mocking local sports associations' new wellness programs, from yoga and meditation to kale chips, with athletes struggling to adapt.
key_facts: The wellness program initiative in local team sports began on September 15, 2023.
Jane "Kale Smoothie" McGillicuddy, a former Pilates instructor, is the new Wellness Director for the Regional Sports Commission.
McGillicuddy introduced 'Savasana Sundays' for the football team.
Coach Randy McPeacenik leads visualization sessions for the local soccer team, chanting "You envision the ball, you are the ball."
The 'Mental Health Half-Time' reportedly replaced traditional pep talks, with coaches spending fifteen minutes on feelings and stress management pamphlets.
Hockey coach Frank "Free Spirit" Sanders has goalies use visualization, which reportedly leads to less stress but more goals scored against them.
Baseball coach Larry "Lotus" Larkin teaches controlled breathing and chakra focus in the batter's box, saying "If you can't center your breath, how can you center a pitch?"
Basketball coach Theo "Thirst Quencher" Thompson serves cucumber and lemon-infused water, while players just want a decent swig of water.
Erica "Energy Flow" Eriksson has her football team practice tai chi, which critics say is incompatible with the speed of the game.
Johnny "Junk Food" Jefferson swapped his pre-game hot dogs for kale chips, helping start the quinoa game-day fuel trend.
Sideline snacks now include more fig bars and fewer nachos.
Stories abound of athletes raiding concession stands for 'real food' or accidentally scoring for the other team while meditating.
